# HALVORSEN & PRICE LLP — Counsel for Pinecrest Senior Living, Inc.
September 29, 2026 · Via email

Re: Your demand dated [session 1] — Juniper Health Staffing / Pinecrest

Counsel:

We represent Pinecrest. Your demand letter asserts (i) $340,000 in unpaid invoices, (ii) $112,000 in conversion fees for seven employees, and (iii) a "tortious interference" claim valued at $410,000. We respond briefly.

1. **Interference.** Pinecrest cannot "interfere" with a contract to which it is a party, and in any event Juniper **consented** to the hires. Your own account manager wrote on February 11, 2026: *"consider the fee waived … as a one-off, you guys have been a great partner. Just keep the RN orders coming."* (copy attached). Your letter states that Juniper "never consented to any direct hire." That statement is contradicted by Juniper's own records. We enclose a draft Rule 12(b)(6) motion directed to the interference count that we will file if you sue on it.
2. **Conversion fees.** Section 3 permits Juniper to waive the fee; it did so. To the extent you contend the waiver covered only two individuals, that is a contract dispute, not a tort.
3. **Invoices.** Pinecrest disputes J-4533 (padded hours; notice given within 15 days) and will pay the undisputed balance of the remaining invoices upon resolution of the conversion-fee issue. Pinecrest reserves all rights.
4. We note your letter threatens suit in the Superior Court. We trust you have reviewed the parties' agreement in full.

Very truly yours, /s/ R. Halvorsen
# DRAFT — DEFENDANT'S MOTION TO DISMISS COUNT III (TORTIOUS INTERFERENCE) UNDER RULE 12(b)(6)
…A party to a contract cannot be liable for tortiously interfering with its own contract (*Ashby v. Caldera Partners*, 212 Col. App. 3d 440 (2019)). Nor can a claim lie for interference with Juniper's at-will relationships with its own nurses where Pinecrest acted with Juniper's express consent (Feb. 11 email, Ex. 1) and for a legitimate business purpose (corporate directive to reduce agency spend, Ex. 2) — justification is a complete defense (*Restatement (Second) of Torts §§766, 767, 773*)…
# Session 1 assessment — 22 October 2026

## Recommendation

Pursue collection and the conversion fees through the agreement's required AAA arbitration process, after a focused demand and document exchange. Do not file the proposed court lawsuit or demand the CEO's $862,000 as presently supported. The $410,000 lost profit item lacks a viable tort theory on this record and appears barred by the agreement's exclusion of consequential damages. The two expressly waived hires reduce the seven-hire fee estimate by $32,000. The client has now identified $3,100 in double-entered June shifts, which must be credited. The present **provisional contract amount is $416,900** before any interest: $336,900 corrected invoices + $80,000 estimated fees. Of that, $265,200 is invoiced without a recorded dispute; the corrected June balance is $71,700 and remains disputed.

## Contract and forum

The January 15, 2024 staffing agreement requires Pinecrest to pay Schedule 1 hourly rates within 30 days of invoice. Late amounts bear 1% monthly interest. Pinecrest must dispute an invoice within 15 days of receipt; otherwise it is deemed accepted. We have invoice due dates, but no receipt dates, time sheets, or billing backup. Thus, the four invoices with no recorded dispute have a strong acceptance argument, but receipt and performance still need proof. The June invoice, J-4533, drew a July 9 objection about allegedly padded shifts. Dolapo now confirms two double-entered shifts worth about $3,100; the balance claimed is $74,800 − $3,100 = **$71,700**. The client's description is approximate, so the exact credit remains to be verified against billing records. The merits of any additional disputed shifts and the objection's timeliness cannot be resolved without the invoice receipt date and shift records. An unobjected invoice is prima facie evidence of debt, subject to defenses. [Account stated and waiver](../../library/columbia_account_stated_waiver.md).

Section 3 bars direct or indirect hiring of Juniper-introduced personnel during the term and for 12 months afterward except on payment of 25% of each person's **first-year annualized compensation**. Juniper may waive the fee in writing. Bell's February 11 email expressly waived the fee for Rosa and Tay “as a one-off.” Bell confirms he intended to waive only those two and never agreed to waive the other five. We cannot demand a fee for Rosa or Tay. Pinecrest may nonetheless argue implied waiver or estoppel for Priya, Luis, and Keisha based on Bell's April and May texts, six-minute call, and lack of a recorded objection. Bell supplies no further details about the call. His denial of a later agreement helps Juniper, but it does not erase the ambiguity in the texts or establish what Lindqvist understood. Anne and Victor have no comparable documented acquiescence. [Account stated and waiver](../../library/columbia_account_stated_waiver.md).

The agreement auto-renews annually and permits termination on 60 days' notice. The May 2 email says Pinecrest will reduce agency use and finish current requests. It does not clearly give 60 days' termination notice or establish an obligation to place future staffing orders. Section 6 excludes consequential damages and leaves unpaid fees and conversion fees uncapped. Section 7 incorporates Exhibit C. Exhibit C.1 requires exclusive AAA Commercial Rules arbitration before one arbitrator in Capital City, Columbia, and delegates arbitrability. Section C.3 gives the prevailing party reasonable attorney fees and costs in arbitration or an action to compel it. The court exception applies only to a claim **solely** collecting undisputed invoices under $25,000; each listed invoice exceeds that amount. Court is available for provisional injunctive relief in aid of arbitration, but no current record supports seeking it. The FAA library describes enforcement, stay, and compulsion of covered arbitration provisions, including delegated arbitrability. [FAA §§2–4](../../library/faa_2_4.md). The fee clause creates real downside if Juniper forces an avoidable motion to compel or loses in arbitration. [Fee shifting and candor](../../library/fee_shifting_and_candor.md).

## Claims and proof

**Invoice collection / breach.** The invoice ledger lists five unpaid invoices totaling $340,000 before correction. The four without recorded objections total $265,200 and are the strongest immediate payment demand. J-4533 was $74,800; deducting the approximately $3,100 double entry gives a provisional $71,700 and a corrected aggregate of $336,900. We should acknowledge the error in the letter, seek the remaining audit details, and not assert that Pinecrest accepted J-4533 or that its objection was late. Late interest is contractual, but the record does not state the calculation convention or whether partial payments or credits exist. Demand it according to the agreement, with a reconciled calculation after ledger verification.

**Conversion fees / breach.** Seven names are listed as hires. Rosa and Tay were expressly waived. Bell says he made no further agreement to waive fees. For the other five, the CEO's $64,000 average is an unverified proxy, not each person's first-year annualized compensation. Illustrative math: 5 × 25% × $64,000 = **$80,000**. The actual claim is 25% of the proven first-year annualized compensation for each of Priya, Luis, Keisha, Anne, and Victor, subject to any established waiver or estoppel defense. Hire dates, compensation records, and individual introduction evidence remain unavailable from the client. The three hires discussed in texts carry greater litigation risk; Bell's express “one-off” limit and denial of a later agreement support Juniper, but his later responses are ambiguous. [Account stated and waiver](../../library/columbia_account_stated_waiver.md).

**Tortious interference / lost account profits.** The record shows Pinecrest cutting agency use under a corporate mandate. It does not show an agreement to maintain future orders, an improper act inducing a third party to breach, or support for $410,000 of net lost profit. Pinecrest cannot tortiously interfere with its *own* contract with Juniper. A theory based on Juniper's at-will personnel would require improper means and faces consent and legitimate-business-justification defenses, particularly given the written waiver and later texts. [Tortious interference](../../library/columbia_tortious_interference.md). The contract excludes consequential damages, which is how the projected account-profit item appears on this record. We should not assert this claim or include it in the demand. Pleading a claim without a non-frivolous basis and misstating the waiver would also raise candor concerns. [Fee shifting and candor](../../library/fee_shifting_and_candor.md).

## Arithmetic and open proof

| Item | Arithmetic | Present treatment |
|---|---:|---|
| Invoices without recorded dispute | $68,400 + $71,250 + $66,100 + $59,450 = **$265,200** | Demand payment, subject to account reconciliation |
| Original J-4533 | **$74,800** | Ledger amount before known correction |
| Known June double entry | **−$3,100 approximately** | Credit; exact shift-level amount unverified |
| Corrected J-4533 | $74,800 − $3,100 = **$71,700 approximately** | Request audit and backup; preserve remainder |
| Corrected invoices | $265,200 + $71,700 = **$336,900 approximately** | Subject to exact credit and reconciliation |
| Seven-hire spreadsheet estimate | 7 × 25% × $64,000 = **$112,000** | Overstates claim by including two written waivers |
| Five unwaived-hire estimate | 5 × 25% × $64,000 = **$80,000** | Provisional; actual compensation unknown |
| Spreadsheet lost profits | **$410,000** | Exclude |
| Revised provisional total | $336,900 + $80,000 = **$416,900 approximately** | Includes disputed $71,700; excludes interest |
| Stronger immediate subset | $265,200 + $80,000 = **$345,200** | Fee part still requires compensation and waiver proof |

The remaining unknowns are whether the ledger reflects other credits or payments; exact June shifts and credit amount; invoice delivery dates, time records, and any completed audit; individual hire dates, introduction evidence, and annualized compensation; the contents of the six-minute call beyond Bell's denial of any agreement; any further termination correspondence; and a precise interest calculation. The client has no additional information on these points. They are proof gaps, not facts to fill by assertion. The proposed letter requests records from Pinecrest and reserves reconciliation.
# Draft demand letter — 22 October 2026

**Via email and certified mail**  
Hanna Lindqvist, Administrator  
Pinecrest Senior Living, Inc.

Re: Juniper Health Staffing, LLC — unpaid invoices and conversion fees

Dear Ms. Lindqvist:

We represent Juniper Health Staffing, LLC concerning Pinecrest's obligations under the January 15, 2024 Staffing Services Agreement. Juniper's ledger shows five unpaid invoices originally totaling **$340,000**:

| Invoice | Amount | Due date |
|---|---:|---|
| J-4411 | $68,400 | April 30, 2026 |
| J-4452 | $71,250 | May 31, 2026 |
| J-4490 | $66,100 | June 30, 2026 |
| J-4533 | $74,800 | July 31, 2026 |
| J-4571 | $59,450 | August 31, 2026 |
| **Total** | **$340,000** | |

The four invoices other than J-4533 total **$265,200**. Juniper's records show no dispute notice for those four. Please pay that amount within 14 days of this letter, or identify any payment, credit, or specific objection with supporting records. The agreement also provides 1% monthly interest on late amounts; Juniper reserves a reconciled claim for interest.

We acknowledge your July 9 email disputing J-4533 on the ground that several June shifts appeared padded. Juniper has identified two shifts double-entered on that invoice, totaling **approximately $3,100**. We credit that amount, reducing the present claim on J-4533 from $74,800 to **approximately $71,700**, subject to confirming the exact shift-level amount. Please provide the completed audit, any other specific shifts and amounts challenged, and supporting time or attendance records within 14 days. Juniper will reconcile any additional documented errors promptly and reserves its claim to the balance properly due.

Pinecrest also directly hired seven people from Juniper's roster, according to Juniper's records. Marcus Bell's February 11 email expressly waived the conversion fees for **Rosa M. and Tay W.** as a one-off. Juniper therefore makes **no fee demand for those two**. Bell confirms he did not agree to waive fees for any later hire. The agreement calls for a fee equal to 25% of first-year annualized compensation for each other introduced person hired during the protected period. Juniper presently identifies **Priya S., Luis F., Keisha B., Anne O., and Victor H.** as the five remaining hires. At an illustrative $64,000 annual compensation per person, the estimate is **5 × 25% × $64,000 = $80,000**; the contractual amount must be calculated from each person's actual first-year annualized compensation. Please provide hire dates, positions, and compensation information for those five, or your own fee calculation, within 14 days. If Pinecrest contends that any later fee was waived, please identify the specific communication and circumstances. Juniper reserves its response after reviewing that information.

The present **provisional contract total is approximately $416,900**: $265,200 in four invoices without a recorded dispute + approximately $71,700 on the disputed June invoice after the known credit + an estimated $80,000 in five conversion fees. It is subject to the exact June correction, any further invoice audit findings, actual compensation, any established defenses, and reconciliation of payments or credits; it excludes contractual interest. Juniper is willing to discuss a prompt resolution once the records above are exchanged.

The agreement requires arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association before a single arbitrator in Capital City, Columbia, and provides for prevailing-party attorneys' fees and costs. If we cannot resolve the matter, Juniper will pursue the contract claims in that forum. Please respond within 14 days of this letter and preserve invoice, shift, hiring, compensation, and related communications records.

Sincerely,

Counsel for Juniper Health Staffing, LLC
